goal: Help the developer build/deploy the Windows MSIX output for the Windows target framework instead of a plain .NET target.
must_include: Notices that the project has both `net8.0` and `net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0`, so Visual Studio can be trying to launch the non-Windows target that cannot produce an AppX recipe.
Tells them to select the Windows Machine / `net8.0-windows...` debug target before F5 or publishing.
Suggests removing the plain `net8.0` TFM from the app project if it exists only for tests/shared code, or moving shared code to a separate library.
Includes clearing stale `bin`, `obj`, and `.vs` state or recloning only as cleanup after fixing/confirming the selected Windows target.
must_not: Treats the missing `.appxrecipe` as a file that should be hand-created.
Recommends changing the MAUI app to an unpackaged Windows executable as the primary fix.
Says a signing certificate is always the root cause without checking the selected target framework.
acceptable_alternatives: Use `dotnet publish -f net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0 -c Debug` to force the Windows target outside Visual Studio.
Create a fresh solution or clear VS caches after ensuring the Windows target is selected, if the IDE state is corrupt.
Keep the plain `net8.0` target only in a separate class library referenced by the MAUI app.
solved: The answer directs the developer to build/launch the Windows TFM so the appx recipe is generated and explains what to do with the extra plain TFM.
partial: The answer suggests cleaning/recloning or changing OutputType but misses the selected non-Windows target framework shown by the project file.
notes: The source thread has multiple workarounds; this fixture makes the target-framework selection visible and gradeable.
